name: Network by tiers
description: The solution's definition, recorded results and selection first; then its metric and cascade, problems, ideals, queued findings, public evidence and implementations; then its parent briefly, its children and dependencies by purpose, interface and selected arm, and its dependents by what they rely on. A solution with children adds how they combine. Sections fill a budget in tier order and a cut is named. Knowledge items are offered beside the prompt as candidates; without a retriever of the caller's own, the reference retriever (knowledge.select) picks those the situation bears on.
advantages: Nothing is written per solution; the deciding records (a lost result, a finding) are read first; the budget keeps the closest records when space is short. Selected because: it passes every free case, including those the definition_only baseline misses.
disadvantages: A record that is linked by no column (a finding with no solution or candidate column, a note in prose) is not reached; reading staleness costs a git call per arm.

name: The solution's record alone
description: BASELINE: the solution's own row and nothing connected to it, cut to the budget. It is what a pass reads when no network forms its prompt.
advantages: The smallest prompt; free and instant.
disadvantages: Holds none of the results, findings, parent or children, so it misses every verdict that depends on them.

name: Every knowledge item written in
description: BASELINE: the same prompt with every knowledge item of the solution written into it in the no-retriever order, inactive ones labelled.
advantages: Nothing the solution knows is left out.
disadvantages: Hands a pass items that do not bear on the situation, and contradicted or expired ones beside current ones.

name: No knowledge
description: BASELINE: the same prompt with no knowledge item at all.
disadvantages: Misses the assumption, lesson or person's words a verdict depends on.
